'''Roderich D. Süssmuth''' (born March 6, 1971<ref name="ac"/> in [[Tübingen]]) is a German chemist and biochemist.

== Life ==
Roderich Süssmuth studied chemistry and biochemistry at the [[Eberhard Karls University of Tübingen]] from 1990 to 1996. In 1999, he received his doctorate under Günther Jung in Tübingen with a dissertation entitled ''Isolation, structural elucidation, and synthesis of microbial metabolites from Amycolatopsis mediterranei, Staphylococcus epidermidis, and Streptomyces lividans''.<ref name="ac">{{Cite journal |date=July 12, 2010 |title=Roderich D. Süssmuth |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/ange.201002150 |department=Autoren-Profil |journal=[[Angewandte Chemie]] |volume=122 |issue=30 |pages=5154–5154 |doi=10.1002/ange.201002150 |issn=0044-8249 |lang=de|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

During a postdoctoral stay at the [[Scripps Research Institute]] in La Jolla, California, United States, from 2000 to 2001, he worked with [[Richard A. Lerner]] and [[Carlos F. Barbas]] on catalytic antibodies and organocatalysis. As an Emmy Noether Research Fellow (DFG) from 2001 to 2004, he completed his habilitation in chemistry and biochemistry at the University of Tübingen.{{Citation needed|date=March 2026}}

In 2004, he was appointed Associate Professor of Biological Chemistry at [[TU Berlin]]. In 2008, he was appointed to the Rudolf Wiechert Professorship of Biological Chemistry at TU Berlin.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Süssmuth |first=Roderich D. |last2=Mainz |first2=Andi |date=March 27, 2017 |title=Nicht‐ribosomale Peptidsynthese – Prinzipien und Perspektiven |journal=Angewandte Chemie |language=en |volume=129 |issue=14 |pages=3824–3878 |doi=10.1002/ange.201609079}}</ref>

In 2020, he was named a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] (FRSC){{Citation needed|date=March 2026}} and an honorary member of the [[Israel Chemical Society]].{{Citation needed|date=March 2026}} 

In 2022, he was admitted to the Confraternity of Santa Maria dell'Anima in Rome.{{Citation needed|date=March 2026}}

== Work ==
During his career, Roderich Süssmuth worked in the field of peptide synthesis, addressing current research questions from both a chemical perspective (natural product synthesis) and a biological perspective, particularly with regard to new classes of active compounds with activity against fungi, bacteria, and viruses. Compounds derived from plant-pathogenic bacteria such as ''[[Xanthomonas albilineans]]'' play an important role, including albicidin, which is an inhibitor of plant gyrase and also a highly potent antibacterial agent.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Cociancich |first1=Stéphane |last2=Pesic |first2=Alexander |last3=Petras |first3=Daniel |last4=Uhlmann |first4=Stefanie |last5=Kretz |first5=Julian |last6=Schubert |first6=Vivien |last7=Vieweg |first7=Laura |last8=Duplan |first8=Sandrine |last9=Marguerettaz |first9=Mélanie |last10=Noëll |first10=Julie |last11=Pieretti |first11=Isabelle |last12=Hügelland |first12=Manuela |last13=Kemper |first13=Sebastian |last14=Mainz |first14=Andi |last15=Rott |first15=Philippe |date=January 19, 2015 |title=The gyrase inhibitor albicidin consists of p-aminobenzoic acids and cyanoalanine |url=https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25599532/ |access-date=March 24, 2026 |pages=195-197 |doi=10.1038/nchembio.1734 |first16=Monique |last16=Royer |first17=Roderich D |last17=Süssmuth |journal=[[Nature Chemical Biology]] |volume=11 |issue=3}}</ref>

He elucidated the structure of the antibacterial compound albicidin, investigated its biosynthesis, developed the total synthesis of the peptide, and studied a range of bacterial resistance factors, mostly from plant-associated bacteria.<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlelanding/2023/sc/d3sc00955f |title=Transcription activation by the resistance protein AlbA as a tool to evaluate derivatives of the antibiotic albicidin |date=May 17, 2023 |volume=14 |pages=5069–5078 |doi=10.1039/D3SC00955F |issn=2041-6539 |issue=19}}</ref> Another example is the recent elucidation == Awards ==
{{More citations needed|section|date=March 2026}}
* 2000: Feodor Lynen Fellowship of the [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation]]
* 2002: Emmy Noether Fellowship of the German Research Foundation (DFG)
* 2002: Friedrich Weygand Prize of the Max Bergmann Circle e.V.
* 2003: Young Scientist Award for Natural Product Research of DECHEMA e.V.
* 2003: Eli Lilly Lecture Award
* 2006: Lecturer Fellowship from the [[German Chemical Industry Association]] (VCI)
* 2010: Sigma Aldrich Lecture, Lunteren, Netherlands
* 2013: Visiting Professorship at Ben Gurion University of the Negev, Israel
* 2014: Van Arkel Chair at Leiden University, Netherlands
* 2020: Recipient of the Max Bergmann Medal for outstanding achievements in the field of peptide natural products<ref>{{cite web |title=Max-Bergmann-Medaille |url=http://www.max-bergmann-kreis.org/max-bergmann-medaille.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210429205601/http://www.max-bergmann-kreis.org/max-bergmann-medaille.html |archive-date=April 29, 2021 |access-date=April 29, 2021 |website=Max Bergmann Kreis e.V. |lang=de}}</ref>
